pc.t: Since Jan. 1, 2023, anyone 19 or older (18 for active, retired or honorably discharged military and law enforcement) who is not prohibited may carry a handgun without a permit.

AL.ht: Alabama recognizes any valid out-of-state permit (Ala. Code 13A-11-85).
AL.vt: A person who may carry without a permit may keep a loaded handgun in a vehicle.
AL.pl: Without the consent of the person in charge: police, sheriff and highway patrol stations; jails and detention facilities; inpatient psychiatric facilities; courthouses and buildings where a county commission or city council is meeting; school, college and professional athletic events (unless you have a valid permit); and buildings with guards or security screening at every entrance. Private property needs the owner's consent.
src: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency, Gun Laws
Jefferson County Sheriff, Permit-less Carry Law (2023)

pc.t: Anyone 21 or older who may legally possess a firearm may carry concealed or openly without a permit. Out-of-state permits issued to people under 21 are not valid in Alaska.

AK.ht: Alaska honors a valid permit from any state, but only for holders 21 or older, with no exceptions (AS 18.65.748).
AK.it: Alaska requires you to tell an officer right away that you are carrying a concealed handgun when the officer contacts you on official business (AS 11.61.220).
src: Alaska DPS, Concealed Handgun Permits and Reciprocity

pc.t: Permitless carry, open or concealed, for adults 21 and older who are not prohibited.

AZ.ht: Arizona recognizes valid permits from other states if you are legally present in Arizona (residency not required), not prohibited under Arizona law, and your permit is valid in the issuing state (A.R.S. 13-3112).
AZ.it: No general duty to inform, but in a business that serves liquor you must show your permit to an officer on request (up to a $300 civil penalty).
src: Arizona Senate, Concealed Carry Laws (2022 brief)

pc.t: Arkansas law allows carry without a license; officials and courts have read it as permitless carry for adults not prohibited. Many travelers still rely on a license.

AR.ht: Since August 16, 2013, Arkansas acknowledges every concealed handgun license lawfully issued by another state.
src: Arkansas State Police, Concealed Handgun Carry Licensing

CA.ht: California does not recognize carry licenses from other states. Since 2025 some counties accept CCW applications from nonresidents.
CA.vt: Handguns: unloaded and in a locked container (the trunk counts). Long guns: unloaded. Ammunition separate is safest.
CA.mag: Magazines over 10 rounds: illegal to bring into California, buy, make or sell (Cal. Penal Code 32310).
CA.aw: Assault weapons as defined by California are banned, including many common rifles and some pistols.
CA.x: Bringing ammunition into California generally requires going through a licensed vendor for residents. Many cities add their own rules.

CO.ht: Colorado honors permits only when the holder is 21 or older AND a resident of the issuing state, proven by a matching driver license or ID. Nonresident permits are not honored.
CO.vt: A person who may lawfully possess a handgun may carry it in a private vehicle for lawful protection (C.R.S. 18-12-105(2)(b), 18-12-204(3)(a)).
CO.mag: Magazines over 15 rounds: illegal to sell, transfer, or possess if acquired after July 1, 2013 (C.R.S. 18-12-302).
CO.aw: New 2025 law (SB25-003) adds a permit-to-purchase system for certain semiautomatic firearms with detachable magazines, beginning in August 2026.
CO.x: Denver, Boulder and some other cities have their own rules on carry and certain firearms.
src: Colorado Bureau of Investigation, CHP Reciprocity

CT.ht: Connecticut does not honor other states' permits. Nonresidents may apply to the State Police for a nonresident Connecticut State Pistol Permit.
CT.vt: Only federal safe passage (18 U.S.C. 926A): unloaded, locked away, passing through. Do not stop longer than necessary.
CT.x: Even transporting a handgun generally requires a Connecticut permit unless you are covered by 926A.
src: Connecticut State Police, Pistol Permit FAQ

DE.ht: Delaware honors both resident and nonresident licenses from the listed states. The published list is dated for January 2025 to January 2026 and shows no pending removals.
DE.mag: Magazines over 17 rounds: banned (11 Del. C. 1468, 1469).
DE.x: A permit to purchase is required for in-state handgun purchases.

DC.ht: D.C. honors no other license. D.C. issues its own concealed carry license to nonresidents.
DC.vt: Federal safe passage only (unloaded, locked, not accessible). D.C. requires registration for possession.
DC.pl: Large areas of D.C. are federal property where carry is prohibited (18 U.S.C. 930, federal parks rules).

pc.t: Permitless concealed carry for anyone 21 or older (younger for servicemembers and honorably discharged veterans) who meets Florida's license eligibility criteria, including nonresidents who live in the United States (Fla. Stat. 790.01, 790.015). Florida's open-carry ban was struck down by a state appeals court in 2025; check current status before carrying openly.

FL.ht: Florida honors a valid carry license issued to you by your state of residence, any state, if you are 21 or older (Fla. Stat. 790.015(1)(b)).
FL.vt: A handgun securely encased or not readily accessible may be kept in a private vehicle (Fla. Stat. 790.25).

pc.t: Permitless carry for "lawful weapons carriers" 21 and older (18 if active or honorably discharged military).

GA.ht: Georgia recognizes licenses from the listed states. Because anyone 21 or older who is not prohibited can carry in Georgia without a license, most visitors do not need one.

HI.ht: Hawaii does not honor any out-of-state license.
HI.vt: Anyone bringing a firearm into Hawaii must register it and submit it for inspection with the county police chief within 5 days of arrival (of the person or the firearm, whichever is later). Nobody under 21 may bring a firearm into Hawaii.
HI.x: Flying in with a firearm triggers registration rules. Talk to a Hawaii lawyer first.

pc.t: Anyone 18 or older who is a U.S. citizen or current member of the U.S. Armed Forces, and not disqualified from a license for a reason other than age, may carry concealed without a license. A loaded handgun may be carried concealed in a vehicle under the same rules.

ID.ht: Idaho recognizes concealed weapons licenses from other states; carry the license on you at all times while carrying (Idaho Code 18-3302(5)(g)).
src: Idaho Attorney General, Concealed Weapons FAQ

IL.vt: A nonresident with a valid carry license from their home state may keep a loaded concealed handgun in the vehicle while traveling through Illinois. If you leave the vehicle, lock the firearm inside the vehicle or a locked container. Everyone else: broken down, not immediately accessible, or unloaded and fully enclosed in a case (a closed glove box or console that fully encloses it counts).
IL.mag: Magazines over 10 rounds (long guns) and over 15 rounds (handguns): banned (720 ILCS 5/24-1.10), with narrow exceptions.
IL.aw: Assault weapons: banned (Protect Illinois Communities Act, 720 ILCS 5/24-1.9). Chicago and Cook County add their own bans.
IL.it: If an officer asks, disclose that you have a concealed firearm and show your license.
src: Illinois State Police, Transport Your Firearm Legally (2025)

pc.t: Permitless carry (2022) for adults 18 and older who are not prohibited.

IN.ht: Indiana recognizes handgun licenses issued by other states or foreign countries, according to their terms, while the holder is not an Indiana resident (IC 35-47-2-21(b)).
src: Indiana State Police FAQ, Does Indiana honor licenses from other states?

pc.t: Since July 1, 2021 no permit is required to carry a handgun in Iowa for anyone not prohibited by state or federal law. A permit still helps with the federal school-zone law.

IA.ht: Iowa gives "universal recognition" to valid permits issued by other states to people who are not Iowa residents (Iowa Code 724.11A).

pc.t: Permitless carry for adults 21 and older who are not prohibited.

KS.ht: Kansas recognizes a valid license from any state or D.C. held by a non-Kansas resident 18 or older. Kansas residents need a Kansas license.
src: Kansas Attorney General, Out-of-State License Recognition

pc.t: Anyone over 21 who may lawfully possess a firearm may carry concealed without a license, including visitors from other states and countries.

KY.ht: Kentucky recognizes valid concealed carry licenses issued by other states (since July 15, 1998).
KY.pl: Same places a license holder may not carry (KRS 237.110, 527.020), plus places banned by federal law.
src: Kentucky State Police, Permitless Carry FAQ

pc.t: Anyone 18 or older who is not prohibited from possessing a firearm may carry a concealed handgun without a permit (La. R.S. 14:95(M)). Permitless carriers follow the same restrictions as permit holders.

LA.ht: Louisiana honors permits from the listed states for holders 21 or older (La. R.S. 40:1379.3(T)). Visitors 18 or older can also carry under permitless carry.
LA.it: Louisiana requires you to tell an officer you have a concealed handgun when the officer approaches you in an official capacity, and to show your permit if you have one (La. R.S. 40:1379.3(I), applied to permitless carry by R.S. 14:95(N)).

pc.t: Permitless concealed carry for adults 21 and older (18 for active or honorably discharged military).

ME.ht: Maine honors resident permits from the listed states (25 M.R.S. 2001-A(2)(F)). Anyone 21 or older can also carry under permitless carry.
ME.x: 72-hour waiting period on firearm purchases in Maine (2024).
src: Maine State Police, Concealed Handgun Reciprocity

MD.ht: Maryland honors no out-of-state license. It issues a wear-and-carry permit to nonresidents.
MD.vt: Federal safe passage only: unloaded, locked, out of reach, passing through.
MD.mag: Magazines over 10 rounds: illegal to sell, buy, or bring into Maryland.
MD.pl: Long list of sensitive places after 2023 law (SB 1), plus a default ban on carry onto private property open to the public is enjoined in part. Check before you stop.

MA.ht: Massachusetts has no reciprocity with any state. Nonresidents may apply for a nonresident License to Carry through the Firearms Records Bureau.
MA.vt: Federal safe passage only. Massachusetts law is strict even for possession; do not stop with a firearm unless licensed there.
MA.mag: Magazines holding more than 10 rounds (or more than 5 shotgun shells) are banned unless made before Sept. 13, 1994.
MA.aw: Assault-style firearms: banned (2024 law expanded the ban).
src: Mass.gov, Firearms License and Transaction FAQ

MI.ht: Michigan honors a concealed carry license issued to a resident of the issuing state, by any state. Nonresident licenses are not honored, and Michigan residents need a Michigan license.
MI.vt: Without an honored license, handguns must be unloaded and in a closed case in the trunk, or, if no trunk, not readily accessible.
MI.it: License holders must tell an officer right away that they are carrying when stopped (MCL 28.425f).

hc.CO: Issued or renewed on or after Aug. 1, 2024
hc.MA: Issued or renewed on or after Aug. 1, 2024

MN.ht: Minnesota honors permits from the listed states.
MN.vt: Without an honored permit: handguns unloaded and in a closed case or the trunk; long guns unloaded and fully cased.
src: Minnesota DPS, Permit to Carry Reciprocity

pc.t: Mississippi does not require a license to carry a pistol in a holster, sheath, purse, handbag, briefcase or fully enclosed case, and anyone over 18 may keep a concealed firearm in a motor vehicle (Miss. Code 97-37-1). Adults 21 and older who may lawfully possess a firearm can carry without a permit; check the statute before relying on this if you are 18 to 20.

MS.ht: Mississippi recognizes valid, unexpired licenses to carry concealed pistols issued by other states.

pc.t: Permitless carry for adults 19 and older (18 for military) who are not prohibited.

MO.ht: Missouri recognizes concealed weapons permits from every state that issues them.
src: Missouri Attorney General, Concealed Carry Reciprocity

pc.t: Montana's concealed-carry offense does not apply to anyone eligible to possess a firearm under state or federal law (Mont. Code 45-8-316(3)), so eligible adults may carry concealed statewide without a permit.

MT.ht: A permit from another state is valid in Montana if you carry it with photo ID and the issuing state runs a criminal background check before issuing (Mont. Code 45-8-329).

pc.t: Since Sept. 2, 2023 anyone 21 or older who is not prohibited may carry concealed, residents and nonresidents alike.

NE.ht: Permits are no longer needed to carry in Nebraska. The State Patrol's reciprocity list is used only for Nebraska permit applications.

NV.ht: Nevada honors permits from the listed states (list effective July 1, 2026). Not valid once you become a Nevada resident.
NV.vt: Open carry is generally legal without a permit, and a loaded handgun may be kept in a vehicle; concealed carry needs an honored permit.

pc.t: Permitless carry for adults 18 and older who are not prohibited.

NH.ht: New Hampshire recognizes licenses from states that recognize its own (RSA 159:6-d); the State Police lists the states above. No license is needed to carry in New Hampshire for anyone not prohibited.
src: New Hampshire State Police, Pistol and Revolver Licensing

NJ.ht: New Jersey has no reciprocity with any state. Nonresidents may apply for a New Jersey Permit to Carry a Handgun.
NJ.vt: Federal safe passage only: unloaded, locked, out of reach, and keep moving. New Jersey has arrested travelers who stopped.
NJ.mag: Magazines over 10 rounds: possessing one is a fourth-degree crime (N.J.S.A. 2C:39-1y, 2C:39-3(j)).
NJ.x: Hollow-point ammunition is restricted outside the home and range.
src: New Jersey State Police, Concealed Carry FAQ

NM.ht: New Mexico honors licenses from the listed states.
NM.vt: Without a license, a loaded handgun may be carried in a private vehicle, and loaded open carry is generally legal.
NM.x: Albuquerque and Bernalillo County have issued emergency orders in the past restricting carry in some places.
src: New Mexico DPS, Concealed Carry Licenses

NY.ht: New York does not recognize other states' licenses. Nonresidents may apply for a New York license; residency is not required, and New York City requires its own.
NY.vt: Federal safe passage only: unloaded, locked, out of reach, and keep moving. Airports in the New York area have arrested travelers.
NY.pl: Sensitive places where even license holders may not carry include public transportation and transit facilities and Times Square, among many others (Penal Law 265.01-e). A gun left in a vehicle must be unloaded and locked in a secure storage container; New York City requires guns unloaded, cased and out of sight.
src: New York State, Concealed Carry Law FAQ

NC.ht: North Carolina honors any valid out-of-state concealed handgun permit (G.S. 14-415.24).
NC.vt: Without an honored permit, a handgun may be carried openly in a vehicle (in plain view); concealed requires a permit.
NC.it: Permit holders must tell an officer they have a permit and a concealed handgun when approached or addressed, and show the permit and ID on request (G.S. 14-415.11(a)).
NC.pl: Law enforcement and correctional facilities; space occupied by state or federal employees, including courthouses; schools (a permittee may leave a handgun in a locked vehicle on campus); demonstrations; federal-prohibited places; businesses posted against concealed carry; any time you have been drinking.
src: North Carolina DOJ, Concealed Handguns Reciprocity

pc.t: Permitless concealed carry for adults 18 and older who are not prohibited and who carry a valid driver license or ID from their state of residence.

ND.ht: North Dakota honors licenses from other states (N.D.C.C. 62.1-04-03.1).
ND.it: If carrying without a license, you must tell an officer you have the firearm at any in-person contact.
src: North Dakota Attorney General, Constitutional Concealed Carry

pc.t: Permitless carry (2022) for adults 21 and older who are not prohibited.

OH.ht: Ohio honors a nonresident's valid concealed handgun license from any state.
OH.it: Since 2022, only if an officer asks.
src: Ohio Attorney General, Concealed Carry Reciprocity

pc.t: Permitless carry for adults 21 and older (18 for military) who are not prohibited.

OK.ht: Oklahoma recognizes valid handgun licenses issued by other states (21 O.S. 1290.26). Since Nov. 1, 2019, Oklahoma has constitutional carry, so most visitors do not need a license.

OR.vt: Without an Oregon license, a handgun in a vehicle must be unloaded and not readily accessible; open carry is legal in most places but some cities ban loaded carry.
OR.mag: Measure 114 (2022) would ban magazines over 10 rounds and require a permit to buy a gun. It is not in effect: the Oregon Supreme Court has not ruled, and a 2026 law (HB 4145) delays both parts to Jan. 1, 2028.

PA.ht: Pennsylvania honors licenses from the listed states only for holders 21 and older who live in the issuing state.
PA.vt: Without an honored license, a firearm in a vehicle must be unloaded. Philadelphia requires a license even for open carry.
src: Pennsylvania Attorney General, Concealed Carry Reciprocity

RI.ht: Rhode Island does not generally recognize other states' permits, but someone with a valid out-of-state carry license who is only passing through Rhode Island on the way to another state is exempt (R.I. Gen. Laws 11-47-8). Nonresidents who hold a license from their state may apply to a Rhode Island licensing authority.
RI.vt: With a valid license from another state you may carry while passing straight through. Without one, use federal safe passage: unloaded, locked, out of reach.
RI.aw: Sale of assault weapons banned (2025 law, effective 2026).
src: Rhode Island Attorney General, Bruen Guidance

pc.t: Permitless carry, open or concealed, since March 2024 for adults 18 and older who are not prohibited.

SC.ht: Permits are not required to carry in South Carolina.
SC.vt: A firearm may be stored anywhere in a vehicle.
SC.pl: Law enforcement and correctional facilities; courthouses while court is in session; polling places on election day; government meetings; school and college athletic events; daycares and preschools; churches without permission; medical facilities without authorization; another person's home without permission; places posted with a no-weapons sign.

pc.t: Permitless carry for adults 18 and older who are not prohibited.

SD.ht: South Dakota recognizes valid permits issued by other states without a formal agreement.
src: South Dakota Secretary of State, Concealed Carry FAQ

pc.t: Permitless carry of handguns for adults 21 and older (18 for military) who are not prohibited.

TN.ht: Tennessee treats a facially valid handgun, firearms or weapons permit from any other state as a Tennessee permit, for handguns only; carry the permit at all times (T.C.A. 39-17-1351(r)).

pc.t: Permitless carry of a handgun, open in a holster or concealed, for anyone 21 and older who is not prohibited, including visitors (Penal Code 46.02).

TX.ht: Texas honors licenses from the listed states by agreement or proclamation.
TX.it: License holders must show their license and ID when asked for ID by an officer; permitless carriers have no duty to inform.
TX.pl: Penal Code 46.03 and 46.035: polling places, courts, racetracks, secured airport areas, bars (51% signs), school events, and places posted with 30.05, 30.06 or 30.07 signs.

pc.t: Since May 5, 2021, anyone 21 or older who may lawfully possess a firearm may carry concealed without a permit, with some exceptions (Utah Code 76-10-523(5)).

UT.ht: Utah honors a concealed firearm permit issued by any other state or county (Utah Code 76-10-523(3)).
src: Utah DPS, Permit-less Concealed Carry (HB 60) FAQ

pc.t: Vermont has never required a permit to carry. Adults who are not prohibited may carry.

VT.ht: Vermont issues no permits and requires none.
VT.mag: Magazines over 10 rounds (long guns) or 15 rounds (handguns): illegal to possess, buy, sell or bring into Vermont unless lawfully possessed on or before April 11, 2018 (13 V.S.A. 4021). Out-of-state residents may bring them only for sanctioned shooting competitions.

VA.ht: Virginia honors every state's permit if you are 21 or older, carry photo ID, and show both on demand.
VA.vt: Without a permit, a handgun may be kept secured in a container or compartment in a private vehicle (Va. Code 18.2-308(C)(8)). Open carry is generally legal.
VA.x: Virginia's 2026 legislature took up new firearm restrictions; check for any changes in effect.
src: Virginia State Police, Reciprocity and Recognition

hc.MT: Enhanced permit only, not the restricted permit for ages 18-20
hc.SD: Unrestricted Enhanced and Gold permits only

WA.ht: Washington honors licenses from the listed states (list updated July 10, 2026).
WA.vt: Without an honored license, a loaded pistol in a vehicle is illegal; carry it unloaded.
WA.mag: Magazines over 10 rounds: manufacture, sale and import banned (RCW 9.41.370).
WA.aw: Sale and import of assault weapons banned (RCW 9.41.390).
src: Washington Attorney General, Concealed Pistol License Reciprocity

pc.t: Anyone 18 or older who is a U.S. citizen or legal resident and is not prohibited may carry a concealed deadly weapon without a license (W. Va. Code 61-7-7(c)).

WV.ht: West Virginia honors licenses from states that recognize West Virginia's, by governor notice or written agreement, for nonresidents 21 or older who carry the license (W. Va. Code 61-7-6a). Most visitors can carry without a license anyway.

WI.ht: Wisconsin honors permits from the listed states for nonresidents 21 and older. Wisconsin residents need a Wisconsin license.
WI.vt: Without an honored license, a handgun in a vehicle must be in plain view or unloaded and cased; long guns must be unloaded.

pc.t: Since July 1, 2021 any U.S. resident who may legally possess a firearm may carry concealed without a permit.

WY.ht: Wyoming honors licenses from other states.
src: Wyoming DCI, Concealed Firearm Permit FAQ
